question: Sapna invested ₹21,300 on simple interest, partly at 14% per annum and partly at 11% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 3 years, then find the sum invested at 14% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Simple Interest and Time are equal for two investments, the principal is inversely proportional to the rate of interest.

Ratio of investments = P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 11 : 14

Total ratio parts = 11 + 14 = 25 parts

25 parts = ₹21,300 ⇒ 1 part = 21300 ÷ 25 = ₹852

Sum invested at 14% (P₁) = 11 parts = 11 × 852 = 9372

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,372.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total investment = ₹21,300

Rate 1 (R₁) = 14% p.a., Time 1 (T₁) = 3 years

Rate 2 (R₂) = 11% p.a., Time 2 (T₂) = 3 years

Simple Interest 1 (SI₁) = Simple Interest 2 (SI₂)

**Formula Used:**

SI = P × R × T ÷ 100

 
 Total = ₹21,300
 
 

 

 
 
 Part 1 (x)
 14% p.a. | 3 Years

 
 Part 2 (21300 − x)
 11% p.a. | 3 Years
 
 

 

 
 
 SI₁ = SI₂

**Calculations:**

Let the sum invested at 14% p.a. be x.

Then the sum invested at 11% p.a. will be (21300 − x).

According to the condition that the interest from both investments is equal:

⇒ (x × 14 × 3) ÷ 100 = ((21300 − x) × 11 × 3) ÷ 100

Canceling out 3 and 100 from both sides:

⇒ 14x = 11 × (21300 − x)

⇒ 14x = 234300 − 11x

⇒ 14x + 11x = 234300

⇒ 25x = 234300

⇒ x = 234300 ÷ 25

⇒ x = 9372

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,372.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Simple Interest Rule

When a total sum is divided into multiple parts such that their Simple Interests are strictly equal, the ratio of the invested parts is P₁ : P₂ : P₃ = (1 ÷ R₁T₁) : (1 ÷ R₂T₂) : (1 ÷ R₃T₃).

Equal Amount Rule

If the final amounts (Principal + SI) obtained from multiple parts are equal, the ratio of the invested parts is P₁ : P₂ = 1 ÷ (100 + R₁T₁) : 1 ÷ (100 + R₂T₂).

Difference between SI and CI

For 2 years, the absolute difference between CI and SI on a certain principal sum is given by D = P(R ÷ 100)². For 3 years, the difference formula extends to D = P(R ÷ 100)² × ((300 + R) ÷ 100).
